author: reek
body: A field read twice in one call, with a string literal argument between the two reads, must give the same answer both times.

author: reek
body: It did not. The emitter caches a field access in the register it loaded it into, so a second read of `b.items` in the same expression reuses that register instead of loading again. `emit-text-lit` writes RAX with a hardcoded mov-ri64 before it calls alloc-temp, and alloc-temp only evicts the register it hands out -- so the literal destroyed RAX while the cache went on claiming `b.items` was still there. The second read then used RAX, which by then held the address of the literal, and `list-length` returned the LITERAL's length word.

author: reek
body: The literal must stay LONGER than the list is, or the walk stays in bounds and the test passes while broken. "read-text" is nine characters; the list is three.

author: reek
body: The empty-literal line was written as a control and is not one: `""` is still a text literal, still writes RAX, and returned 0 -- its own length word. Any literal triggers this, so the only honest control is the direct read, which never had a literal to cross.
